transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. You should switch it off and unplug it immediately. A burning odour usually points to lint buildup on the heating element (which can smoulder) or a mechanical part like a belt rubbing against something hot. Both are fire risks. Once you have unplugged the machine, I would suggest checking two things: first, is the fluff filter in the door full of lint? Second, was the load you were drying very small (like one item) or overloaded? Please do not try to use it again until a qualified engineer has inspected it.
I've switched it off at the wall already?? The filter is very full, I haven't cleaned it for a few weeks. Not sure about the load size, sorry. Is that what's causing it??

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, an extremely full fluff filter is very likely the cause. When lint builds up, it can get sucked past the filter and coat the heating element or fan housing; as these parts heat up, the lint smoulders and creates a burning smell. Because this presents a fire risk, the machine must not be used again until a qualified engineer has inspected it to ensure no damage has occurred to internal components.
